title: 8-player survival Pong, built with Opus: the arena loses a wall every time someone dies
author: Nehekhara
selftext:
Eight players, one side each. Miss the ball and your wall is gone, so the arena shrinks and gets faster as it empties. Last one alive wins.



Dying doesn't bench you though. Eliminated players come back as saboteurs and start dropping hazards onto the arena (pegs, gravity wells, spinning bars) on a cooldown. So the survivors are getting squeezed by the players they just knocked out, and the endgame gets messy in a good way.



Built with Opus. canvas 2D, no engine + antics SDK for multiplayer

  
Try it (fills with bots, so you get a full 8-player match even solo): [antics.gg/p/side-out-94df7d](http://antics.gg/p/side-out-94df7d)

  
Disclosure: antics is my own platform. It just hosts the game and runs the multiplayer.

replies.author: Nehekhara
replies.body: Global consistency for the ball (deterministic sim + re-stamp at every change of authority), local authority for your own paddle, and every divergence heals in half a ping. So yes, on someone else's screen a fast-moving paddle can look a step behind its own bounce, because the sprite is eased while the ball follows the truth. But that's the trade done right: the picture absorbs the lag so the physics never has to. If your paddle was there, the save counts, at any ping, on every screen.

comments.author: SunriseMilkshake
comments.body:
Love the concept, but I feel towards the end the momentum drastically increased and didnt give a fair shot of the remaining players to defend themselves. Players could either vote which type of advantage to acquire for the next rounds, or  I'd do one or a mix of the following:

1. Give players 'survivors buffs' like being able to duplicated their paddle for .25 seconds upon activation (like click or tap or something easy). That way they can cover more ground. Or a 'slow mo mode' that lasts .3-.5 seconds. Or lets a player get a 'sticky paddle' that lets them hold on to the ball for 1 second and relaunch it from another position.  
1.5 Or give players ways to sabotage each other, like spawning a force field for .3 seconds that pushes the ball away in an unexpected way, or various 'curses', like 'heavy ball' that makes the ball be attracted to the last paddle that bounced the ball as if it was the largest gravity well in play. Maybe a "slow curse" could make the next persons paddle that hits the ball move 25% slower until their next hit.  
2. Give very small bumpers/deflectors for the very corners so that people don't feel cheated that the ball got really close to the corners  
3. Allow randomly assigned users to delete 1 or more sabotages/traps, but with only 2-5 seconds to decide to keep the pace going

Just stuff that evens the playing field at the end, increases the stakes, and makes players feel like they have more control over their victory.

comments.author: Ok_Environment_4992
comments.body: The saboteur mechanic is what sells this. Most survival-pong ideas just shrink the arena and call it a day, but letting dead players actively mess with survivors means nobody's sitting out bored. That's the kind of design choice that keeps a party game alive past the first round.
